items.title: Interview #95 Jeff McMillan, founder of McMillanAI and former CAIO at Morgan Stanley
items.summary: Jeff McMillan, founder of McMillanAI and former Chief AI Officer at Morgan Stanley, breaks down why most of today's 70,000 AI companies will not survive: anyone can build a polished product in a weekend, so the only durable edge is proprietary data and deep domain expertise. He explains why AI will reprice traditional software rather than kill it, and why handing out Copilot and expecting ROI is like giving fifth graders calculators and asking why they aren't accountants yet. Jeff also dives into why over 90 percent of enterprise problems could run on a model from two years ago, comparing frontier spend to driving a Ferrari in circles in a Walmart parking lot, and why token leaderboards are as absurd as rewarding whoever used the most electricity. Finally, he shares why human in the loop breaks down at 20,000 agents, and what managers must learn to supervise people and machines working side by side. items.title: Bridging the Gap Between AI Builders and Domain Experts
items.summary: Everyone is racing to build one agent that can do everything. Justin Schroeder , co-founder of Standard Agents , thinks the future looks more like thousands of tiny ones. Ahead of his talk on domain-specific agents at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America, he explains why tightly scoped agents might be the smarter bet, even if it feels like a step back toward the single-purpose machine learning models of a few years ago. We dig into standards as metadata you pin to an agent, so that it shows up with everything it needs in its harness. Then we test the idea against the obvious objection: if a big model can already handle the task, why scope down at all? The answer covers forcing functions, a microservices mindset for agent design, and small agents that quietly check issues or unread messages every five minutes. It also covers the surprise $1K bill waiting for anyone who leaves their agents running. Then it turns into a proper debate. Our host is 99% sure the agent marketplace will never happen, and Justin arrives with a counter that might change his mind (hint: think about where your skills come from). Along the way, we cover agents as tools versus a big-brain router and how anyone keeps track of a thousand agents. We also talk about why the people who know what agents can do and the people who know what they need still have to meet in the middle. items.title: Sean Gorman & Marc Prioleau: zephr.xyz
items.summary: In this episode, Sean Gorman and Marc Prioleau discuss the innovative work at Zephr on improving GPS accuracy, building open-source spatial data models, and the future of location technology. They explore how these advancements can transform navigation, mapping, and autonomous systems.
